newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore budget generally praised by chamber.
newsitem.headline: Singapore budget generally praised by chamber.

text.p: Singapore's budget for 1997/98 won general praise on Friday from the Singapore International Chamber of Commerce, but it criticised the removal of a tax exemption on provident fund payments for foreigners.
The budget had been presented to parliament earlier in the day by Finance Minister Richard Hu.

"The various incentives for...broadcasting, telecommunications, the logistics industry, and in particular...for the financial sector, will certainly help to further enhance Singapore as one of the world's leading business centres," the chamber said in a statement.

However, it said: "The removal of the (Central Provident Fund) tax exemption for foreigners will make it increasingly difficult to attract the high quality foreign talent that is essential for regional HQ operations."
The net result would be companies increasing salary packages for that pool of talent, adding to operating costs and making the affected companies less competitive.
The chamber also said that while it was pleased Hu recognised business costs needed to be contained, it was somewhat disappointed no new incentives were announced to address the problem areas.
